profile: Makes packaging materials from wood fibre, and converted packaging, for consumer brands, retailers and industry. It also sells pulp, other bio-based materials, sawn timber and engineered wood, while managing company-owned and associated forests and providing wood and energy-related services.

otherClaims.label: Debt and other claims, less cash

summary: Stora Enso Oyj (STERV.HE, NASDAQ Helsinki) makes fibre-based packaging materials, converted packaging, pulp, bio-based materials, sawn timber and engineered wood, and owns or manages forests. The share price was €10.1 on 26 October 2026, against market capitalisation of €8bn and enterprise value of €11.6bn. In this Valuatum market report dated 26 October 2026, the analysis reads the price as a market allocation across the businesses rather than as a target or recommendation. The company’s 2028 analysts’ forecast is revenue of EUR 10.1bn and operating profit of EUR 929m, while end-2026 forecast debt and other claims, less cash, reduce the business total by €4.6 per share.

Forests are the largest component at €8.1 per share, based on 75% of the company’s reported forest value of EUR 8.5bn and representing 55% of the EUR 14.7 per share contributed by the businesses before claims. Packaging materials contributes €3.7 per share at 9.6x 2028 operating profit; Biomaterials contributes €1.7 at 8.2x; Wood products €0.7 at 8.2x; and Packaging solutions €0.5 at 7.4x. Together the businesses contribute €14.7 per share, while debt and other claims, less cash, subtract €4.6, producing the €10.1 share price. The four mills are read at about 9x forecast operating profit, versus listed peers at about 10x.

The mills trade below peer comparisons because several forecasts require operational recovery: Packaging materials must move from a 2.9% 2025 margin to 7% in 2028, Biomaterials from 9.6% to 13%, Wood products from −0.1% to 4%, and Packaging solutions from 1.4% to 5%. The key evidence is Oulu’s planned 750,000 tonnes of capacity during 2027, the Swedish forest separation planned for the first half of 2027 subject to shareholder approval, the Central European wood review, pulp prices and margins. The mean of 16 analysts’ targets is €11.5 (MarketScreener), with a range of €9.0–€13.5.

thesis.title: What you pay for
thesis.text: Forests account for €8.1 per share, or 55% of the €14.7 contributed by the businesses before claims. The other four businesses are priced at about 9x their 2028 forecast operating profit, while debt and other claims, less cash, subtract €4.6 per share.

thesis.title: Why below peers
thesis.text: The four mill businesses cost about 9x 2028 operating profit against listed peers at about 10x. Oulu is not yet at full output, Packaging solutions faces excess capacity, and Biomaterials and Wood products remain exposed to weak pulp, timber and mill economics.

thesis.title: What to watch
thesis.text: The immediate operating test is Oulu reaching its 750,000-tonne annual capacity during 2027. The larger structural event is the Swedish forest separation, planned for the first half of 2027 subject to a shareholder vote, followed by wood margins and the Central European review.

valuePools.name: Forests
valuePools.economics: reference value: 75% of EUR 8.5bn reported forest value · 2028 operating profit of EUR 343m in the split · published readings 68%–82%
valuePools.text: Forests are the largest part of the share price, contributing €8.1 per share and €6.4bn of enterprise value in the split. That equals 75% of the company’s reported forest value of EUR 8.5bn and 55% of the EUR 14.7 per share generated by the businesses before debt and other claims. The holdings include forests, leased land and associated-company interests. The Swedish forest company planned for separation would contain more than 1.2 million hectares, valued by the company at approximately EUR 5.8bn at the end of 2025. The segment sold EUR 1.3bn to outside customers in 2025, supplied 35.3 million cubic metres and earned adjusted operating profit of EUR 317m. The 75% reading sits between published readings of 68% from Danske Bank, 80% from Handelsbanken and 82% from SB1 Markets, although those readings cover different holdings. The shareholder vote and any listing would test the value directly.

valuePools.name: Packaging materials
valuePools.economics: 9.6x 2028 operating profit · 2028 operating profit of EUR 304m · peers 8.5x–12.1x, median 10.3x
valuePools.text: Packaging materials sells board made from fresh and recycled fibre to packaging makers and brand owners. It generated EUR 4.3bn of outside sales in 2025 and delivered 2.852 million tonnes of consumer board and 1.296 million tonnes of containerboard. The split assigns EUR 304m of 2028 operating profit, a 7% margin on EUR 4.6bn of outside sales, and reads the price at €3.7 per share, or 9.6x forecast operating profit. That is below the peer median of 10.3x but within the peer range of 8.5x–12.1x. The principal operational test is Oulu, a EUR 1bn conversion with 750,000 tonnes of annual capacity; first deliveries began in Q2 2025 and full capacity is targeted during 2027. The valuation also reflects peer weakness: Metsä Board reported a −9.5% 2025 operating margin and MM Board & Paper −3.65%. The market therefore requires the forecast margin recovery to become visible.

valuePools.name: Biomaterials
valuePools.economics: 8.2x 2028 operating profit · 2028 operating profit of EUR 159m · industry median 9.5x
valuePools.text: Biomaterials sells pulp and other fibre-based materials to manufacturers serving paper, packaging and other products. Outside sales were EUR 1.2bn in 2025, with 2,280,191 tonnes delivered against annual pulp capacity of 2.5 million tonnes. The split assigns EUR 159m of 2028 operating profit, a 13% margin on EUR 1.2bn of sales, and €1.7 per share at 8.2x forecast operating profit. That is below the industry median of 9.5x and within quartiles of 6.3x and 12.5x. The 2025 adjusted operating profit was EUR 110m, or a 9.6% margin, so the price assumes improvement from a weak end to 2025, when fourth-quarter sales fell 17% year on year. Skutskär’s fiberline 3 softwood-pulp closure during Q3 2026 and a EUR 19m fluff-pulp investment change the production base. Pulp prices and demand in Europe and China, together with mix and volume, determine whether the 13% margin is reached.

valuePools.name: Wood products
valuePools.economics: 8.2x 2028 operating profit · 2028 operating profit of EUR 66m · industry median 9.5x
valuePools.text: Wood products sells sawn timber and other wood-based building products to construction customers and distributors. Outside sales were EUR 1.6bn in 2025, with 4,256 thousand cubic metres delivered against sawing capacity of 5.4 million cubic metres. The split assigns EUR 66m of 2028 operating profit, a 4% margin on EUR 1.7bn of sales, and €0.7 per share at 8.2x forecast operating profit. The multiple is below the industry median of 9.5x and within the 6.3x–12.5x quartile range. The business made an adjusted operating loss of EUR 2m in 2025, or a −0.1% margin, so the forecast requires a clear recovery. Stora Enso no longer reports the business separately, is reviewing seven Central European sawmills and three cross-laminated timber mills, and confirmed the permanent closure of the Veitsiluoto sawmill with about 60 redundancies. Fuller remaining mills, a result from the review and stronger building demand are the evidence needed for the 4% margin.

valuePools.name: Packaging solutions
valuePools.economics: 7.4x 2028 operating profit · 2028 operating profit of EUR 57m · industry median 8.4x
valuePools.text: Packaging solutions converts fibre into corrugated and other packaging for retail, e-commerce and industrial customers. It sold about EUR 1bn to outside customers in 2025 and earned adjusted operating profit of EUR 14m, a 1.4% margin. The split assigns EUR 57m of 2028 operating profit, a 5% margin on EUR 1.1bn of sales, and €0.5 per share at 7.4x forecast operating profit. That is below the industry median of 8.4x, although the industry quartiles range from 6.0x to 11.5x. Overcapacity held margins down in 2025, while customer-mix and cost actions protected the remaining profit. The July 2026 sale of the German corrugated-board operations removed assets from a low-profit business, but no sale price was stated. The market’s reading depends mainly on whether the remaining plants can spread fixed costs across more output. Further closures or disposals and a sustained move above the 1.4% margin would provide the clearest evidence that the forecast 5% margin is becoming credible.

coreAnalysis.heading: What the price pays for
coreAnalysis.text: The share price is primarily a forest holding rather than a collection of similarly valued mills. Forests contribute €8.1 per share, equal to 55% of the €14.7 per share attributed to the businesses before debt and other claims. The calculation counts the forests at 75% of the EUR 8.5bn value reported by the company, producing forest enterprise value of EUR 6.4bn. The remaining four businesses contribute €6.6 per share in total: Packaging materials €3.7, Biomaterials €1.7, Wood products €0.7 and Packaging solutions €0.5. Their operating-profit multiples are 9.6x, 8.2x, 8.2x and 7.4x respectively on 2028 forecasts. Debt and other claims, less cash, subtract €4.6 per share, leaving the €10.1 market price. The split therefore says that the share price is made up of a large asset-value component, a smaller collection of forecast-dependent mill profits and a substantial claims deduction. The evidence also separates reported asset value from profit multiples: forests are read against published asset readings, while the mills are read against 2028 operating profit. The interpretation of the share price depends first on how investors value the forests and then on whether the mills deliver the margins embedded in the forecast.

coreAnalysis.heading: Why the price is below peers
coreAnalysis.text: The four mill businesses are priced at about 9x 2028 operating profit, compared with listed peers at about 10x, because their forecasts require recoveries that have not yet been demonstrated. Packaging materials must move from a 2.9% 2025 margin to 7% in 2028, with Oulu’s 750,000 tonnes of annual capacity targeted to run during 2027. The market has evidence for caution: Metsä Board reported a −9.5% 2025 operating margin and MM Board & Paper −3.65%. Biomaterials must rise from a 9.6% 2025 margin to 13% while pulp demand and prices were weak in Europe and China. Wood products must recover from a −0.1% margin while the Central European sawmill and building-solutions review remains unresolved and Veitsiluoto is closing. Packaging solutions must move from 1.4% to 5% despite excess capacity, with the German corrugated operations sold in July 2026. These are business-specific reasons for the discount rather than a simple industry-wide comparison. The peer evidence is also not uniform: Packaging materials is compared with three listed peers, while Biomaterials and Wood products use industry quartiles because fewer than three peers could be read. The share-price composition therefore reflects operational uncertainty, capacity changes and forecast margin expansion rather than a single group-level multiple.

coreAnalysis.heading: What to watch
coreAnalysis.text: The first structural event is the Swedish forest separation, planned for the first half of 2027 and subject to shareholder approval. Approval and a listing would give the largest part of the businesses a daily market price, testing the company’s reported forest value of EUR 5.8bn for the planned Swedish company and the 75% reading used here. Without approval, the forests remain inside the group and continue to be interpreted through broker readings ranging from 68% to 82%, which cover different holdings. The first operating test is Oulu: quarterly delivery volumes should move towards 750,000 tonnes during 2027, while Packaging materials’ outside-sales margin should progress from 2.9% in 2025 towards 7% in 2028. Biomaterials requires pulp prices, demand and mix to lift the margin from 9.6% towards 13%, with Skutskär’s closure and fluff-pulp investment providing a changed base. Wood products needs a result from the Central European review, fuller mills after Veitsiluoto and an improvement from a −0.1% margin towards 4%. Packaging solutions needs evidence that capacity reduction and customer-mix actions can lift the margin from 1.4% towards 5%. These events determine whether the share price remains dominated by asset value or reflects stronger mill earnings.

risks: Forest separation failure (Forests): shareholder approval may not be obtained, leaving the largest business inside the group without a daily listed price; the early warning is the General Meeting vote planned before the first half of 2027.
Oulu under-delivery (Packaging materials): the new line may remain below its 750,000-tonne capacity, leaving the forecast 7% 2028 margin unsupported; the early warning is quarterly delivery volume.

Pulp weakness and changed mix (Biomaterials): lower prices, weak European and Chinese demand and the Skutskär closure may keep the margin near 9.6% rather than 13%; the early warning is quarterly pulp prices, demand and outside-sales margin.

Capacity and asset review (Wood products): the Central European review or Veitsiluoto closure may fail to improve utilisation and margins; the early warning is post-closure deliveries against 1,118 thousand cubic metres in Q1 2026 and the outside-sales margin.
Excess capacity (Packaging solutions): plant under-utilisation may keep the margin near 1.4% rather than 5%; the early warning is quarterly outside-sales margin and further capacity actions.
catalysts: Swedish forest vote and separation (near-term/medium-term, Forests): approval and a planned first-half-2027 listing would provide a daily market price for the largest asset pool.
Oulu reaching capacity (medium-term, Packaging materials): delivery of 750,000 tonnes during 2027 would show that start-up costs are ending and the 7% forecast margin is within reach.
Central European review outcome (near-term, Wood products): a sale or closure of high-cost, low-margin units would clarify the route towards a 4% 2028 margin.
Pulp recovery and Skutskär mix improvement (medium-term, Biomaterials): firmer prices, stronger demand and successful fluff-pulp output would support progress from a 9.6% margin towards 13%.

Further capacity reduction (medium-term, Packaging solutions): additional plant closures or disposals would allow fixed costs to be spread across more output and support progress from a 1.4% margin towards 5%.

faqs.q: What is Stora Enso Oyj’s share price made of?
faqs.a: Forests contribute €8.1 per share, Packaging materials €3.7, Biomaterials €1.7, Wood products €0.7 and Packaging solutions €0.5. The businesses total €14.7 per share before debt and other claims, less cash, subtracts €4.6, leaving a €10.1 share price.

faqs.q: Why does Stora Enso trade below its peers?
faqs.a: The four mill businesses cost about 9x 2028 operating profit against listed peers at about 10x. The comparison reflects required margin recovery, including Packaging materials moving from 2.9% in 2025 towards 7% in 2028 and Packaging solutions from 1.4% towards 5%.

faqs.q: What do analysts expect for Stora Enso?
faqs.a: The mean of 16 analysts’ targets is €11.5, with a range of €9.0–€13.5 (MarketScreener). Analysts forecast 2028 sales of EUR 10.1bn and operating profit of EUR 929m.

faqs.q: What should Stora Enso investors watch?
faqs.a: The main events are the shareholder vote and planned first-half-2027 Swedish forest separation, Oulu’s progress towards 750,000 tonnes during 2027, pulp prices and margins, the Central European wood review and operating margins across the mills.

faqs.q: How does Valuatum’s market report work?
faqs.a: The analysis keeps analysts’ forecasts of 2028 sales of EUR 10.1bn and operating profit of EUR 929m, splits forecast profit between businesses, compares each business with peers using EV/EBIT and reads today’s €10.1 share price back into the businesses. Forests are counted at 75% of the reported EUR 8.5bn value.
